The relief sought for is to abstain the respondents three and four from enter upon the petitioners lands and drawing the stringing corridor lines (Row) (Wire above the Lands) across the land belonging to the petitioners situated in S.Nos.118/7B and 118/8 of the 1st petitioner S.Nos. 17/2 and 17/3 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis of the 2nd petitioner, S.No.18/1 of the 3rd petitioner,
S.No.22/7 of the 4th petitioner, S.Nos.18/2A and 2B of the 5th petitioner, S.No.17/1 of the 6th petitioner, S.Nos.83/1, 83/2 and 83/3 of the 7th petitioner, S.No.83/4 of the 8th petitioner, S.No.83 of the 9th petitioner, S.No.76/1, 5 and 6B of the 10th petitioner, S.No.76/6A, 8, 9, 10 and 12A of the 11th petitioner S.Nos.114/3, 4 and 5 of the 12th petitioner, S.No.119/1 of the 13th petitioner,
S.No.124/2A of the 14th petitioner, S.No.124/1 of the 15th petitioner and the S.No.123/8 of the 16th petitioner.
2. Mr.P.Wilson, learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the respondents 3 and 4 would contend that the high tension tower has already been erected and lines are also in operation.
Strings are already fixed and some of the land owners have already received compensation as fixed by the competent authorities.
Few land owners are yet to receive the compensation.
But those land owners also have given letters for receiving the compensation as determined by the authorities under the Indian Telegraphic Act, 1885.

3. Therefore, the relief sought for in the present writ petition to abstain the respondents are not surviving and the petitioners are at liberty to approach https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis the authorities to receive the compensation or seeking enhancement of compensation by approaching the District Collector under the Indian Telegraphic Act, 1885 as the case may be.
4. With these liberty, this Writ Petition stands disposed of.
No costs.
